items.title: Leslie Gourse interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996
items.q: I went out to their house, I met her

ctx.x: Did you get to know Jillean somewhat?

Yes. I went out to their house, I met her, and the thing that struck me was her eyes. You know she was not the young, beautiful kid. As I mentioned she was a mature woman but beautiful in a new way. Her eyes were so full of light, and I could see why Joe was charmed forever about Jillean. We’re all getting a little older, but she is just a charming woman. Beautiful eyes and just a lovely, lovely woman. A lovely woman. Kind.

I’ve been struck by the dignity that many of these veteran African-American musicians carry with them, and when you hear about — in fact they’re not that forthcoming with some of the stories about traveling in the south and so forth, but when you do hear some of them they weathered it so well. It seems like they don’t have a lot of negative, they refuse to be negative or carry that with them — I think — for the most part.
